attributes.extent: ~40 square miles of fused salt, in sheets, blisters and ridges
features: green-black glass sheets that ring underfoot
blister-domes, some man-high, hollow and thin-walled
the detour: the Road's only bend, added a century after the survey
hazards: cuts hide, hoof and boot; a team driven onto it is lamed in an hour
lightning walks it every summer - it is still being made
no shade, no water, no landmarks once you are in it
attributes.position: ~2 days east of the Dry Ferry; the beacon line detours 1.5 days around its north edge
uses: saltglass shards are cut for eye-slits and lamp lenses at Bell Harrow
a shortcut across it saves 3 days and has never once been worth it

name: The Glass Lees
summary: Two days east of the Dry Ferry the crust changes colour and then stops being crust: forty square miles of saltglass, fused green-black in sheets and blisters where lightning walks the plain every summer and has done for two hundred years. It rings underfoot like a struck pot and it cuts hide, hoof and boot, so nothing crosses it and the beacon line goes around. Cut a shard and hold it up and the whole plain goes the colour of a bottle.
